selected_frontier.reason: Accepted target productive Python/_sqlite3 path remained SQLite 3.45.1 in WAL-relevant release scope; a published Ubuntu patchset probe had just eliminated the unproven-backport escape for package 3.45.1-1ubuntu2.7. The read-only root-anchor verifier was then found to enforce filesystem trust metadata but not the already-defined V5 semantic anchor schema.
duplicate_avoidance: Existing V5 guard already defines FRANK_SQLITE_RUNTIME_TRUST_ANCHOR_V1 and validates manifest/runtime fields
Existing package-provenance and published-patchset workflows already cover backport discovery

hypothesis: The read-only productive-path verifier could report OBSERVED_PRODUCTIVE_RUNTIME_MATCHES_ROOT_ANCHOR for a root-owned anchor with the correct runtime triplet even when the anchor protocol/manifest identity was invalid, because anchor_match compared only sqlite_version, sqlite_source_id and library_sha256.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Filesystem root ownership plus the three exact runtime fields might be sufficient because protocol/manifest validation occurs elsewhere in the V5 launcher, making the read-only probe merely a narrower runtime observation rather than a trust decision.

go_out_of_box.name: ANCHOR_SCHEMA_CONFUSION
go_out_of_box.description: Replicate the current three-field anchor_match logic locally with correct runtime triplet but protocol=WRONG_PROTOCOL and manifest_sha256=null.
go_out_of_box.interpretation: The read-only verifier's semantic anchor match was fail-open with respect to anchor schema identity.

counterevidence_and_scope.existing_v5_guard: fixed_sqlite_runtime_guard_v5_candidate.py already validates protocol FRANK_SQLITE_RUNTIME_TRUST_ANCHOR_V1, all five required non-empty string fields, SHA-256 syntax, and binds trusted manifest_sha256 to the actual manifest.
counterevidence_and_scope.scope_limit: The read-only workflow does not itself load the V5 manifest, so this repair validates schema identity and runtime triplet but does not claim full launcher/manifest execution-chain acceptance.
counterevidence_and_scope.root_anchor_absence: The accepted target still lacks the OS-owned anchor, so repaired target execution must remain blocked.

change: Require protocol, manifest_sha256, library_sha256, sqlite_version and sqlite_source_id as non-empty strings
Require manifest_sha256 and library_sha256 to be 64-hex SHA-256 text
Expose anchor_schema_trusted and schema_errors in observation/annotation

accepted_target_test.interpretation: Expected fail-closed target result. This validates that the repaired workflow executes on the accepted target; it does not exercise the schema-invalid branch because the root anchor is absent.
